tests.title: Open on an existing root returns its absolute, symlink-resolved path
given: a temp directory T and a symlink L that points at T
tests.when: workspace.Open(L, workspace.Options{}) is called
then: the error is nil
Root() equals filepath.EvalSymlinks(filepath.Abs(L)), i.e. the resolved T
a relative root yields the same absolute resolved path
tests.pseudocode: ws, err = Open(L, Options{}); assert err == nil; assert ws.Root() == EvalSymlinks(T)

tests.title: Open with an empty root uses the symlink-resolved working directory
given: the process working directory is a temp directory reached through a symlink
tests.when: workspace.Open("", workspace.Options{}) is called
then: the error is nil
Root() equals the symlink-resolved os.Getwd()
tests.pseudocode: t.Chdir(L); ws,_ = Open("", Options{}); assert ws.Root() == EvalSymlinks(Getwd())

tests.title: Open keeps a missing root in lexical absolute form without error
given: a path P under a temp directory that does not exist
tests.when: workspace.Open(P, workspace.Options{}) is called, and again with a relative missing path
then: the error is nil
Root() equals filepath.Abs(P) with no symlink resolution
no directory is created
tests.pseudocode: ws, err = Open(P, Options{}); assert err == nil; assert ws.Root() == Abs(P); assert !exists(P)

tests.title: Open returns (nil, error) when the working directory cannot be determined
given: the process working directory has been removed after chdir into it (test skipped on platforms where os.Getwd still succeeds)
tests.when: workspace.Open("", workspace.Options{}) is called
then: the returned *Workspace is nil
the returned error is non-nil and is the underlying os.Getwd error
tests.pseudocode: t.Chdir(d); os.Remove(d); ws, err = Open("", Options{}); assert ws == nil; assert err != nil

tests.title: Open reads no ignore file and starts no subprocess
given: a root containing a .gitignore that is a directory-unreadable trap and a fake `git` first on PATH that records every invocation
IgnoreOptions whose Getenv, Home and GitConfig hooks count their calls
tests.when: workspace.Open(root, opts) is called and nothing else
then: the fake git recorded zero invocations
the Getenv, Home and GitConfig hooks were called zero times
the .gitignore file was not opened (no access recorded)
tests.pseudocode: ws,_ = Open(root, Options{Ignore: counting}); assert gitCalls == 0; assert hookCalls == 0

tests.title: Workspace has no exported fields and Options has exactly one field, Ignore
given: the workspace package
tests.when: reflect inspects workspace.Workspace and workspace.Options, and Open is called with the zero Options
then: Workspace has zero exported fields
Options has exactly one field named Ignore of type IgnoreOptions
Open with the zero Options succeeds and does not set any hook (zero IgnoreOptions)
tests.pseudocode: assert NumExportedFields(Workspace) == 0; assert Options.NumField()==1 && Field(0).Name=="Ignore" && Type==IgnoreOptions

tests.title: Concurrent use of one Workspace gives sequential results and no data race
given: one *Workspace over a tree with nested .gitignore files, run under go test -race
tests.when: for any number of goroutines (1..64) each calling Root, Resolve, Rel, CheckWriteTarget, Ignore, Walk and Ignored on the same workspace with generated paths
then: every goroutine's result equals the result of the same call made sequentially
the race detector reports no race
tests.pseudocode: seq = map(calls, run); parallel(N, calls); assert results == seq

tests.title: Resolve normalizes, joins, resolves symlinks against the deepest ancestor and compares segment-wise
given: a workspace root with an inside symlink to an inside directory, a dangling symlink whose target is inside, and a sibling directory named root+"-evil"
tests.when: Resolve is called with a relative file, a not-yet-existing file, `@rel`, a quoted path, the inside symlink, the dangling link and the sibling path
then: relative and `@`/quoted forms return the contained absolute path with nil error
a non-existing leaf resolves against the deepest existing ancestor
the dangling link resolves to its in-root target
the sibling `root-evil` is refused (segment-wise containment, not prefix)
tests.pseudocode: assert Resolve("a/b.txt") == root+"/a/b.txt"; assert errors.Is(Resolve(root+"-evil/x"), ErrPathNotAllowed)

tests.title: A path resolving outside the root is refused with the workspace path_not_allowed error
given: a workspace root R, a symlink R/out -> outside directory, and an in-root directory D that is swapped for an outward symlink after Resolve
tests.when: Resolve("out/f"), Resolve of an absolute outside path and CheckWriteTarget(D/f) after the swap are called
then: each error satisfies errors.Is(err, workspace.ErrPathNotAllowed)
the text starts with "workspace: path_not_allowed" and names the root R
the text ends with "; use a path inside the workspace (a relative path is resolved against the root)"
CheckWriteTarget re-resolves the whole path and refuses the swapped component
tests.pseudocode: err = Resolve("out/f"); assert Is(err, ErrPathNotAllowed); assert HasPrefix(err.Error(), "workspace: path_not_allowed"); assert HasSuffix(err.Error(), nextStep)

tests.title: Malformed paths are refused with the workspace path_malformed error
given: a workspace and the unknown user name `no-such-user-xyz`
tests.when: Normalize or Resolve is called with "", a path containing a NUL byte, a non-local file:// URL, "~no-such-user-xyz/x", and a chain of 41 symlinks
then: each error satisfies errors.Is(err, workspace.ErrPathMalformed)
each error text starts with "workspace: path_malformed"
tests.pseudocode: for p in bad: err = Resolve(p); assert Is(err, ErrPathMalformed); assert HasPrefix(err.Error(), "workspace: path_malformed")

tests.title: A ~ path with an unresolvable HOME is refused with ErrNoHome
given: HOME and the platform home variables unset so os.UserHomeDir fails
tests.when: Normalize("~") and Normalize("~/x") are called
then: each error satisfies errors.Is(err, workspace.ErrNoHome)
the text starts with "workspace: home directory could not be resolved"
no relative path is returned
tests.pseudocode: unsetenv(HOME); _, err = Normalize("~/x"); assert Is(err, ErrNoHome)

tests.title: Normalize expands home forms and strips @ and quotes exactly as before
given: HOME set to a temp directory H and the current user known
tests.when: Normalize is called with `~`, `~/x`, `~<current user>/x`, `@x` and `"quoted path"`
then: `~` gives H, `~/x` gives H/x, `~user/x` gives that user's home plus /x
`@x` gives `x` and the quoted path loses its quotes
outputs equal the strings recorded from the pre-change tools.Normalize test table
tests.pseudocode: assert Normalize("~/x") == (H+"/x", nil); assert Normalize("@x") == ("x", nil)

tests.title: Rel returns a root-relative path under the root and the input unchanged otherwise
given: a workspace root R
tests.when: Rel is called with R/a/b, R itself, a path outside R and a sibling R+"-evil/x"
then: R/a/b gives "a/b"
outside paths are returned unchanged
the call never panics or reports an error
tests.pseudocode: assert Rel(R+"/a/b")=="a/b"; assert Rel("/elsewhere")=="/elsewhere"

tests.title: File tools fail with result code path_not_allowed for a refused path and leave the file untouched
given: tools.For over a workspace in a temp dir, and an outside file O with known content
tests.when: read_file, write_file and edit_file are called with the absolute path of O and with a path through an outward symlink
then: each result is an error result with code "path_not_allowed"
the message contains the workspace error text starting "workspace: path_not_allowed"
O's content and mtime are unchanged and no new file is created
tests.pseudocode: r = call(write_file, {path:O, content:"x"}); assert r.IsError && r.Code=="path_not_allowed"; assert read(O)==orig

tests.title: IgnoreOptions has the documented fields and NoGlobalExcludes empties the global layer
given: the workspace package
tests.when: reflect inspects IgnoreOptions and NoGlobalExcludes() is called and its GitConfig is invoked
then: IgnoreOptions has Getenv func(string) string, Home func() (string, error) and GitConfig func() string
NoGlobalExcludes().GitConfig() returns ""
a workspace opened with NoGlobalExcludes() ignores nothing on account of a global excludes file present in the environment
tests.pseudocode: assert NoGlobalExcludes().GitConfig() == ""

tests.title: At most one core.excludesFile lookup per workspace, none before first use, including under concurrent first use
given: a workspace opened with a counting GitConfig hook
tests.when: the count is read after Open, then 32 goroutines first use the rules at once through Walk and Ignored, then use them again
then: the count is 0 after Open
the count is exactly 1 after the concurrent first use
the count stays 1 after further walks and Ignored calls
tests.pseudocode: Open(...); assert n==0; parallel(32, ()=>Ignored("a",false)); assert n==1

tests.title: Ignore() returns options whose GitConfig is memoized and reusable without another lookup
given: a workspace opened with a counting GitConfig hook returning a path P
tests.when: opts := ws.Ignore() is obtained, opts.GitConfig() is called three times, then a second workspace is opened with opts and used
then: every GitConfig call returns P
the underlying hook ran at most once in total
the second workspace's rules use P without running the hook again
tests.pseudocode: o = ws.Ignore(); assert o.GitConfig()==P && o.GitConfig()==P; assert n<=1; ws2=Open(root,Options{Ignore:o}); use(ws2); assert n<=1

tests.title: Ignore sources apply in precedence order and the last match wins
given: a global excludes file ignoring *.log, .git/info/exclude ignoring !keep.log, a root .gitignore ignoring build/ and a sub/.gitignore with `!important.log` and `*.tmp`
tests.when: Ignored is called for a.log, keep.log, sub/important.log, build, sub/x.tmp and plain.txt, and Walk visits the tree
then: a.log is ignored by the global layer
keep.log is re-included by the repository exclude file
sub/important.log is re-included by the later .gitignore
build and sub/x.tmp are ignored, plain.txt is not
Walk visits exactly the entries Ignored reports as not ignored
tests.pseudocode: assert Ignored("a.log",false) && !Ignored("keep.log",false) && !Ignored("sub/important.log",false)

tests.title: Nested repositories start a new ignore root, .git is always ignored and .ignore is not a source
given: root .gitignore ignoring *.dat, a nested repository dir sub/repo with its own .git and no .gitignore, and a root .ignore file containing *.txt
tests.when: Ignored and Walk are evaluated for sub/repo/f.dat, sub/repo/.git, .git/config and a.txt
then: sub/repo/f.dat is not ignored because the root .gitignore stops applying at the repository boundary
any path with a .git segment is ignored even with a `!.git` pattern
a.txt is not ignored because .ignore is not read
Walk with IncludeHidden never calls fn for a .git path
tests.pseudocode: assert !Ignored("sub/repo/f.dat",false); assert Ignored(".git/config",false); assert !Ignored("a.txt",false)

tests.title: Walk visits the non-ignored entries under sub with rel relative to sub and the engine rooted at sub
given: a tree with a root .gitignore ignoring *.gen, sub/ with no .gitignore, a global excludes file ignoring *.glob and .git/info/exclude ignoring *.excl
tests.when: Walk is called with sub "", ".", "sub" and the absolute path of sub
then: "" and "." visit the same set
rel is slash-separated and relative to sub
with sub="sub" the root .gitignore pattern *.gen does not apply but the global layer and .git/info/exclude do
the relative and absolute forms of the same sub visit identical sets, equal to the pre-change tools.Walk set recorded for this tree (TestSearchReadsOnlyItsOwnIgnoreSources)
the error is nil
tests.pseudocode: Walk(ctx,"sub",WalkOptions{},collect); assert "x.gen" in got && "y.glob" !in got && "z.excl" !in got

tests.title: Walk refuses a sub outside the root, and a nil receiver, before calling fn
given: a workspace over R, a sibling directory R+"-evil", and a nil *Workspace
tests.when: Walk is called with "../x", an absolute outside path, R+"-evil", "a/../../x", and on the nil receiver with ""
then: each error satisfies errors.Is(err, workspace.ErrPathNotAllowed)
fn is called zero times
an absolute sub inside the root and "a/../b" are accepted
tests.pseudocode: calls=0; err = Walk(ctx,"../x",WalkOptions{},fn); assert Is(err,ErrPathNotAllowed) && calls==0

tests.title: Walk skips hidden entries by default, does not follow symlinks, skips unreadable entries and checks sub lexically
given: a tree with .hidden/f, a symlink to an outside directory, an unreadable directory (skipped on platforms where chmod 000 is not enforced) and a symlink dir inside the root used as sub
tests.when: Walk runs with IncludeHidden false and true
then: dot-prefixed entries are absent with IncludeHidden false and present with true
the symlinked directory's contents are never visited
the unreadable entry produces no fn call and Walk returns nil
a sub that is an in-root symlink to an outside directory is accepted lexically (not resolved) and not refused
tests.pseudocode: assert ".hidden" !in walk(false); assert ".hidden" in walk(true); assert err==nil

tests.title: Walk of a missing sub or a regular file makes no calls and returns nil
given: a workspace with a regular file a.txt and no directory missing/
tests.when: Walk is called with "missing" and with "a.txt"
then: fn is called zero times for each
the error is nil for each
tests.pseudocode: assert Walk(ctx,"missing",o,fn)==nil && calls==0; assert Walk(ctx,"a.txt",o,fn)==nil && calls==0

tests.title: Walk returns the context error at the next entry when cancelled
given: a tree of 100 files and a context cancelled by fn on the 3rd call, plus a context whose deadline has already passed
tests.when: Walk runs with each context
then: with cancellation after the 3rd call, Walk returns context.Canceled and fn is not called for the 4th entry
with the expired deadline Walk returns context.DeadlineExceeded and calls fn zero times
tests.pseudocode: err = Walk(cctx,"",o,fn); assert err==context.Canceled && calls==3

tests.title: Walk honours SkipDir and SkipAll and returns any other fn error
given: a tree with directories d1/ and d2/, each holding files
tests.when: fn returns filepath.SkipDir at d1, filepath.SkipAll at the first file, and a sentinel error E at a chosen entry
then: SkipDir skips d1's contents, visits d2, and Walk returns nil
SkipAll stops the walk and Walk returns nil
E stops the walk and Walk returns exactly E
tests.pseudocode: assert Walk(...SkipDir...)==nil && "d1/f" !in got; assert Walk(...E...)==E

tests.title: WalkOptions has one field, IncludeHidden, and Walk always applies the workspace's own rules
given: a workspace opened with Options.Ignore whose GitConfig names a global excludes file ignoring *.secret
tests.when: reflect inspects WalkOptions and Walk runs over a tree containing x.secret
then: WalkOptions has exactly one field, IncludeHidden of type bool
x.secret is never visited by Walk with either IncludeHidden value
tests.pseudocode: assert WalkOptions.NumField()==1; assert "x.secret" !in walk(true)

tests.title: Ignored matches rel and every ancestor using ancestors' ignore files from the root down
given: root .gitignore `vendor/`, a/.gitignore `*.o` and `!keep.o`, nested repository a/repo/ with .git, and the workspace root
tests.when: Ignored is called with "vendor/x/y.go", "a/b.o", "a/keep.o", "a\\b.o" (backslash separator), "a/repo/z.o" and "vendor" with isDir true
then: a file below an ignored directory is ignored
a/b.o is ignored by the ancestor's .gitignore and a/keep.o is re-included
backslash and slash forms give the same answer
a/repo/z.o is not ignored (a/.gitignore stops applying at the nested repository boundary)
tests.pseudocode: assert Ignored("vendor/x/y.go",false); assert Ignored("a/b.o",false)==Ignored("a\\b.o",false)

tests.title: Ignored reports .git segments as ignored and the root as not ignored
given: a workspace with no ignore files
tests.when: Ignored is called with ".git", "a/.git/config", "x/.git" with isDir true, "" and "."
then: every path with a .git segment returns true
"" and "." return false
tests.pseudocode: assert Ignored("a/.git/config",false); assert !Ignored("",true) && !Ignored(".",true)

tests.title: Ignored fails closed for absolute and escaping paths
given: a workspace over R
tests.when: Ignored is called with an absolute path inside R, "/etc/passwd", "../x" and "a/../../x"
then: each call returns true
tests.pseudocode: for p in [R+"/a", "/etc/passwd", "../x", "a/../../x"]: assert Ignored(p,false)==true

tests.title: A dot-prefixed name is not reported ignored on account of its leading dot
given: a workspace whose rules do not mention .env or .config
tests.when: Ignored is called with ".env", ".config/app.toml" and ".github" with isDir true
then: each returns false
tests.pseudocode: assert !Ignored(".env",false) && !Ignored(".config/app.toml",false)

tests.title: Ignored keeps no cache: an edited .gitignore changes the next answer
given: a workspace over a tree with a/.gitignore containing `*.x` and no other rules
tests.when: Ignored("a/f.x", false) is called, a/.gitignore is rewritten to empty, Ignored is called again, then .git/info/exclude gains `*.x` and it is called a third time
then: the first call returns true
the second returns false
the third returns true
tests.pseudocode: assert Ignored(p)==true; write(gitignore,""); assert Ignored(p)==false; write(exclude,"*.x"); assert Ignored(p)==true

tests.title: Walk from the root visits exactly the WalkDir entries that Ignored reports as not ignored
given: a randomly generated tree without unreadable entries, with nested .gitignore files, negations, nested repositories (.git dirs) and hidden entries, opened with NoGlobalExcludes()
tests.when: for any such tree, ws.Walk(ctx, "", WalkOptions{IncludeHidden: true}, fn) is compared with filepath.WalkDir over the root
then: the set of rel paths Walk visits equals the set of WalkDir entries (excluding the root itself) with Ignored(rel, d.IsDir()) == false
tests.pseudocode: for tree in gen_trees(): visited = walkSet(ws); expected = {rel for rel,d in WalkDir(root) if rel!="." && !ws.Ignored(rel,d.IsDir())}; assert visited == expected

tests.title: tools.For returns the eleven built-ins in order with definitions byte-identical to the pre-change tools.All
given: a workspace opened in a temp dir and definitions recorded from the pre-change tools.All stored under testdata
tests.when: tools.For(ws, tools.Options{}) is called and each tool's name, description, input schema, output schema, guidelines and execution mode are JSON-marshalled
then: the error is nil and the length is 11
the names in order are read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files, find_files, search_files, file_outline, find_symbol, find_references, execute, run_command
the marshalled definitions equal the recorded bytes
the Anthropic golden request in testdata/golden/request_anthropic.json is still produced
tests.pseudocode: ts,err = For(ws, Options{}); assert names(ts)==want; assert marshal(ts)==recorded

tests.title: Every tool's sandbox definition digest is unchanged
given: the digests of the eleven tools recorded before this change in sandbox/internal/tooldigest test data
tests.when: tooldigest.Digest is computed over each tool returned by tools.For
then: each digest equals the recorded pre-change digest
tests.pseudocode: for t in For(ws,Options{}): assert Digest(t) == recorded[t.Name]

tests.title: Index tools are appended after the built-ins and a duplicate name fails
given: a stub tools.Index whose Tools() returns one tool named idx_search, and another whose Tools() returns a tool named read_file
tests.when: tools.For(ws, tools.Options{Index: idx}) is called with each
then: with idx_search the result has 12 tools with idx_search last and no error
with read_file the result is nil and the error is today's duplicate-name error (text recorded from the pre-change tools.All)
tests.pseudocode: ts,err = For(ws, Options{Index: idx}); assert ts[11].Name=="idx_search"

tests.title: tools.For with a nil workspace returns no tools and an error naming the workspace
given: the process working directory is a valid directory
tests.when: tools.For(nil, tools.Options{}) is called
then: the returned slice is nil
the error is non-nil and its text names the missing workspace (contains "workspace")
the working directory is not used as a fallback
tests.pseudocode: ts, err = For(nil, Options{}); assert ts==nil; assert Contains(err.Error(),"workspace")

tests.title: tools.Options has the five fields, the spill dir derives from the root hash, and constructors stay unexported
given: two workspaces opened at the same root and one at another root
tests.when: reflect inspects tools.Options and the default spill directory is computed through tools.For for each workspace, and the exported identifiers of package tools are listed
then: Options has exactly SpillDir, DisableSpill, Env, Symbols and Index
the same root gives the same default spill directory and a different root gives a different one, equal to defaultSpillDir(hash of ws.Root())
no exported identifier of tools is an individual tool constructor
tests.pseudocode: assert fields(Options)==[SpillDir,DisableSpill,Env,Symbols,Index]; assert spill(ws1)==spill(ws2)!=spill(ws3)

tests.title: execute and run_command run in the workspace root
given: tools.For over a workspace at a temp dir R whose process working directory differs
tests.when: execute runs `pwd` and run_command runs the pwd binary
then: both outputs equal ws.Root() (symlink-resolved R)
tests.pseudocode: assert trim(call(execute,{command:"pwd"}).text)==ws.Root()

tests.title: Every tool walk uses the workspace's ignore rules, including non-default ones
given: a workspace opened with IgnoreOptions whose GitConfig points at a global excludes file ignoring secret_*, and a Go tree containing secret_a.go, a nested a/.gitignore ignoring b.go, and ordinary files
an index stub whose candidate set includes secret_a.go and a/b.go
tests.when: find_files, search_files (native and with the index candidate filter), find_symbol (table build then refresh after adding a file), find_references (package load and candidate scan) and References are run
then: none of them returns or reads secret_a.go
none returns a/b.go (nested .gitignore honoured, including by the index-candidate filter)
each walk was made through ws.Walk or ws.Ignored (test seam records the calls), none through the real environment
tests.pseudocode: for tool in tools: assert "secret_a.go" !in output(tool) && "a/b.go" !in output(tool)

tests.title: A tool set built from one workspace runs at most one core.excludesFile lookup across all walks
given: a workspace opened with a counting GitConfig hook and tools.For over it
tests.when: find_files, search_files, find_symbol (build and refresh), find_references and list_files are each called twice
then: the hook ran exactly once in total
tests.pseudocode: run all; assert n==1

tests.title: tools.References returns the same sites as the pre-change method, with default bounds, no cache and no index
given: a small Go module in a temp dir with a declaration and three reference sites, and the site list recorded from the pre-change (*Workspace).References
tests.when: tools.References(ctx, ws, target, tools.ReferenceOptions{}) is called
then: the error is nil
the ReferenceResult equals the recorded result
no reference cache file or index is consulted or created
tests.pseudocode: res, err = References(ctx, ws, target, ReferenceOptions{}); assert err==nil && res==recorded

tests.title: tools.References with a nil workspace returns an empty result and an error
given: a valid target declaration
tests.when: tools.References(ctx, nil, target, opts) is called
then: the ReferenceResult equals the zero value
the error is non-nil
no search or walk was performed
tests.pseudocode: res, err = References(ctx, nil, t, o); assert res.IsZero() && err!=nil

tests.title: tools.References with a path outside the workspace returns ErrPathNotAllowed and an empty result
given: a workspace over R and an outside directory O
tests.when: tools.References is called with opts.Path set to O and to "../x"
then: the ReferenceResult is the zero value
errors.Is(err, workspace.ErrPathNotAllowed) is true
tests.pseudocode: res, err = References(ctx, ws, t, ReferenceOptions{Path:O}); assert Is(err, workspace.ErrPathNotAllowed) && res.IsZero()

tests.title: tools.References stops with the context's error when cancelled
given: a Go tree and an already-cancelled context
tests.when: tools.References(ctx, ws, target, opts) is called
then: the error satisfies errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)
the result is empty
tests.pseudocode: cancel(); _, err = References(ctx, ws, t, o); assert err == context.Canceled

tests.title: Search, SearchIn and CountCandidates keep root-path signatures and results; SearchIn takes workspace.IgnoreOptions
given: a temp tree with ignored and non-ignored matches and results recorded before the change
tests.when: tools.Search(ctx, root, p), tools.SearchIn(ctx, root, p, workspace.NoGlobalExcludes()), a SearchIn with a GitConfig naming a global excludes file, and tools.CountCandidates(ctx, root, p) are called
then: results equal the recorded results
the global excludes file given through the workspace.IgnoreOptions argument is honoured
the signatures compile with root as a string path
tests.pseudocode: assert SearchIn(ctx, root, p, workspace.NoGlobalExcludes()) == recorded

tests.title: ReferenceOptions, ReferenceSite and ReferenceResult keep their fields
given: the field lists of the three types recorded before the change in the exported-API golden
tests.when: reflect inspects the types
then: names, types and order of fields equal the recorded lists
tests.pseudocode: assert fields(ReferenceOptions)==recorded

tests.title: tools declares none of the removed identifiers
given: the non-test and test source files of package tools parsed with go/parser
tests.when: the top-level declarations, struct fields and methods are scanned for Workspace, NewWorkspace, Walk, WalkOptions, IgnoreOptions, NoGlobalExcludes, Normalize, ErrPathNotAllowed, ErrPathMalformed, ErrNoHome, All, Options.Workspace, Options.Ignore and a References method with a Workspace receiver
then: none is found as a type, alias, var, const, func or field
tools.References exists as a plain function
tests.pseudocode: for d in decls(tools): assert d.Name !in removed

tests.title: codesearch.Options declares no Ignore field
given: the codesearch module
tests.when: reflect inspects codesearch.Options
then: no field named Ignore exists
MaxFiles, MaxBytes, MaxBuildTime and TempDir remain
tests.pseudocode: _, ok = TypeOf(Options{}).FieldByName("Ignore"); assert !ok

tests.title: workspace non-test files import only the standard library and doublestar
given: package workspace
tests.when: go list -f '{{.Imports}}' (or go/parser import scan) runs over its non-test files
then: every import is a standard-library path or github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4
no github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go path appears
private copies of the glob wrapper and the hidden-name test exist inside workspace
tests.pseudocode: for imp in imports(workspace): assert isStdlib(imp) || imp==doublestar

tests.title: The internal/policy graph test fails naming the file and import for an offending workspace file
given: a synthetic package directory whose non-test file imports github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/tools, and another whose only offending import is in a _test.go file
tests.when: the policy check function for the workspace import rule is run on each directory
then: for the first, it reports a failure whose text names the offending file and the import path
for the second, it reports no failure (test files exempt)
run on the real workspace package it passes
tests.pseudocode: err = checkWorkspaceImports(dir); assert Contains(err, "bad.go") && Contains(err, ".../tools")

tests.title: tools imports workspace, MatchGlob and ExpandBraces stay in tools, and the root package imports neither
given: the import lists of the root module's packages
tests.when: the imports of tools, workspace and the root agentkit package's non-test files are listed, and tools' declarations are scanned
then: tools imports workspace
tools declares MatchGlob and ExpandBraces
the root agentkit non-test files import neither tools nor workspace
tests.pseudocode: assert "workspace" in imports(tools); assert imports(agentkit) ∩ {tools, workspace} == ∅

tests.title: codesearch.New takes a workspace, builds through ws.Walk and revalidates with its rules, on both platforms
given: a workspace over a temp tree opened with NoGlobalExcludes() and a nested .gitignore, and the Windows stub build target
tests.when: codesearch.New(ws, codesearch.Options{}) is called, the index is built, a new file is added and a .gitignore edit un-ignores another file, then revalidation runs
then: New returns (non-nil tools.Index, nil)
the built file set excludes ignored files
revalidation picks up the added and un-ignored files using the workspace's rules
